statement: In Illinois you change your legal name by filing a Request for Name Change with the circuit clerk, and a judge signs an Order for Name Change granting it.
detail: You fill out a Request for Name Change and an Order for Name Change, file them with the circuit clerk (usually by electronic filing), get a hearing date, and go in front of a judge. If having your court file open to the public would harm your health or safety, you can also file a Motion to Impound. The guide says the laws on adult name change were updated beginning January 1, 2024, and again on March 1, 2025. The guide no longer lists a newspaper publication step. Illinois law also sets a residency requirement and restricts who may file after certain criminal convictions — see the paired eligibility record, which cites the statute itself.

cost.note: Filing fees differ from case to case and county to county — ask the circuit clerk. A fee waiver is available if you qualify.
cost.fee_waiver_criteria: If you cannot afford the fees, you can ask to have them waived.

topic: Illinois name change: residency requirement and who may file
statement: Illinois law (735 ILCS 5/21-101, as amended effective March 1, 2025) lets a resident of Illinois file a petition to change their name in the circuit court of the county where they reside. The petitioner must have resided in Illinois for 3 months at the time of the name-change hearing or the entry of the order granting the change.
detail: The statute page displays two earlier versions of this section, effective July 1, 2024, that required 6 months of residency before filing; the March 1, 2025 version is the latest. The same section restricts who may file. A person convicted of an offense that requires registration under the Sex Offender Registration Act, the Murderer and Violent Offender Against Youth Registration Act, or the Arsonist Registration Act, who has not been pardoned, may not file a name-change petition during the registration period unless they verify under oath that the petition is due to marriage, religious beliefs, status as a victim of trafficking, or gender-related identity as defined by the Illinois Human Rights Act — and a judge may grant or deny that request. A person convicted of a felony whose sentence has not been completed, terminated, or discharged may not file unless pardoned. If the court grants a name change to someone with an unpardoned conviction, a pending charge, or an arrest without a filed charge, a copy of the order goes to the Illinois State Police, which updates its records to show both the new and the former name.

source.title: Illinois General Assembly — 735 ILCS 5/21-101, Change of Name: Proceedings; Parties

statement: Illinois identification can carry a male, female, or X sex designation. To change the sex designation on a driver's license or state ID, you complete a Gender Designation Change form and bring it, with your current Illinois license or ID, to a Secretary of State facility.
detail: You go in person to a Secretary of State facility, and an appointment may be required. The guide does not list a medical-documentation requirement for this change.

cost.note: The guide does not state a separate fee for the designation change. Fees for new and corrected identification are listed on the Secretary of State's website.

timeline.typical: handled in person at a Secretary of State facility; an appointment may be required

source.title: Illinois Legal Aid Online — Updating Sex and Gender Markers on Identification

statement: If you were born in Illinois and have an Illinois birth certificate, you can change the sex designation on it by sending the state health department a signed, notarized Affidavit and Certificate of Correction Request. You can pick M, F, or X.
detail: Since July 1, 2023, state law lets you change the gender on your birth certificate by signing a statement affirming your gender designation or intersex condition. The health department then creates a new birth record. Your old birth certificate and the papers behind the change go into a sealed file.

cost.note: The $15 fee includes one certified copy of the new birth certificate. Extra copies are $2 each if you order them at the same time.

source.title: Illinois Department of Public Health — Gender Change on a Birth Certificate

statement: If you are changing the gender on your Illinois birth certificate and want your name changed at the same time, you must also send a certified copy of your Court Order of Legal Name Change.
detail: Ask for the name change in the second section of the Affidavit and Certificate of Correction Request form. The health department will then make a new birth record with the new sex designation and the new name.

cost.note: The $15 fee includes one certified copy of the new birth certificate. Extra copies are $2 each if you order them at the same time.

topic: Illinois name change for a minor: petitioner, notice, and the best-interest standard
statement: In Illinois, the parent or guardian who has legal custody of a minor signs the petition to change the minor's name. Before the court can order the change, the law requires actual notice and a chance to be heard for any parent whose parental rights have not been terminated, and for anyone who has been allocated parental responsibilities under the Illinois Marriage and Dissolution of Marriage Act.
detail: The court may enter a name-change order for a minor only if it finds, by clear and convincing evidence, that the change is necessary to serve the best interest of the child. The law lists factors the court must consider: the wishes of the child's parents or anyone acting as a parent with physical custody; the wishes of the child and the reasons for them (the court may interview the child, with counsel present); how the child gets along with parents, step-parents, siblings, and step-siblings; and how the child is adjusted to their home, school, and community.

source.title: 735 ILCS 5, Article XXI — Change of Name

topic: Illinois name change for a minor: consent, publication, and fees
statement: Illinois Legal Aid Online says one parent can ask to change a child's name even if the other parent does not agree — the other parent must be legally notified of the case, but the guide does not say the other parent's agreement is required. It also says Illinois law lets a child who is fourteen years of age or older consent to a name change, and that a judge may let a younger "mature" child state their preference too.
detail: If a parent cannot be found or does not respond, the guide says a judge can require service by publication: a notice published in a newspaper in the county once a week for three weeks in a row, with the first publication at least six weeks before the court date. There may be a fee to publish, and some newspapers will honor a fee waiver order, but the guide says they are not required to. A fee is charged to file the case, and the amount varies by county; a family can file an Application for Waiver of Court Fees to ask the judge to waive it. The guide's newspaper-publication step for a minor's case is different from the adult name-change process, which no longer lists a publication step.

cost.note: The filing fee varies by county. A fee waiver is available for families who qualify.

source.title: Illinois Legal Aid Online — Starting a Case to Change a Child's Name

topic: Illinois birth certificate sex designation for a minor
statement: Illinois uses the same Affidavit and Certificate of Correction Request form to change the sex designation on a birth certificate for a minor as for an adult. The applicant must be of legal age to complete the form, or, if the person is not of legal age, their parent, co-parent, or guardian completes it instead.
detail: The form must be signed and notarized either way. If the family also wants a name change at the same time, they must submit a certified copy of the Court Order of Legal Name Change — the health department's page does not say a court order is needed for a gender-designation change by itself, for a minor or an adult.

cost.note: The $15 fee includes one certified copy of the new birth certificate. Extra copies are $2 each if ordered at the same time.
